---
title: "Size and illiquidity"
jupyter: python3
---

We can sort on two characteristics to see, for example, whether the spread
between illiquid and liquid stocks differs across size portfolios. We use
monthly market capitalization and a measure constructed from daily prices
and volume. As in the size chapter, the holding months are January 2000
through December 2002; this is a methods comparison, not a replication of
published estimates.

## From daily data to monthly illiquidity

Following [Amihud (2002)](https://doi.org/10.1016/S1386-4181(01)00024-6),
divide each absolute daily return by daily dollar volume, then average the
ratios. Here we average within each stock-month, require 10 usable days,
and scale by one million for readability. CRSP's
[`dlyprcvol`](https://www.crsp.org/wp-content/uploads/guides/CRSP_US_Stock_%26_Indexes_Database_Guide_Flat_File_Format_2.0.pdf)
approximates dollar volume as price times shares traded. We exclude zero
volume and use only information through the formation month.

```{python}
import polars as pl
from eap_pl import load_parquet

first = pl.date(2000, 1, 1)
last = pl.date(2002, 12, 1)

illiq = (
    load_parquet("dsf_v2", "crsp")
    .filter(
        pl.col("dlycaldt").is_between(first.dt.offset_by("-1mo"), last, closed="left"),
        pl.col("dlydelflg") == "N",
        pl.col("dlyret").is_finite(),
        pl.col("dlyprcvol").is_finite(),
        pl.col("dlyprcvol") > 0,
    )
    .with_columns(
        month=pl.col("dlycaldt").dt.month_start(),
        daily_illiq=1e6 * pl.col("dlyret").abs() / pl.col("dlyprcvol"),
    )
    .group_by("permno", "month")
    .agg(illiq=pl.col("daily_illiq").mean(), days=pl.len())
    .filter(pl.col("days") >= 10)
    .select("permno", "month", "illiq")
)
```

## Align formation and holding months

We apply the same formation screen as in the size chapter. Both
characteristics are measured in month $t$; the return is for month $t+1$.
For the AnomalyLab comparison we keep only rows with a usable holding return
before sorting. As in the size chapter, this complete-case convention is
not a recommended way to form portfolios in a real-time backtest.

```{python}
monthly = (
    load_parquet("msf_v2", "crsp")
    .with_columns(month=pl.col("mthcaldt").dt.month_start())
    .filter(pl.col("month").is_between(first.dt.offset_by("-1mo"), last))
)

formation = (
    monthly
    .filter(
        pl.col("securitytype") == "EQTY",
        pl.col("securitysubtype") == "COM",
        pl.col("sharetype") == "NS",
        pl.col("usincflg") == "Y",
        pl.col("issuertype").is_in(["ACOR", "CORP"]),
        pl.col("primaryexch").is_in(["A", "N", "Q"]),
        pl.col("tradingstatusflg") == "A",
        pl.col("conditionaltype") == "RW",
        pl.col("mthcap") > 0,
    )
    .select("permno", "month", size="mthcap")
    .join(illiq, on=["permno", "month"], validate="1:1")
    .with_columns(month=pl.col("month").dt.offset_by("1mo"))
)

returns = monthly.select("permno", "month", ret="mthret")
stocks = (
    formation
    .join(returns, on=["permno", "month"], validate="1:1")
    .filter(pl.col("ret").is_finite())
    .collect()
)
```

## Sort independently and within size groups

For independent sorts, compute both sets of breakpoints for the full
cross-section each month. For dependent sorts, compute the illiquidity
breakpoints within each size quintile. The dependent sort therefore
compares the relatively illiquid and liquid stocks of similar size.
We use the same linear quantile and right-closed convention as AnomalyLab.

```{python}
def quintile(data, var, by):
    x = pl.col(var)
    cuts = [x.quantile(q / 5, interpolation="linear").over(by) for q in range(6)]
    if data.select(
        pl.any_horizontal(a >= b for a, b in zip(cuts, cuts[1:])).any()
    ).item():
        raise ValueError(f"Non-unique quintile edges for {var}")
    return 1 + pl.sum_horizontal((x > cut).cast(pl.Int32) for cut in cuts[1:-1])

by_size = stocks.with_columns(size_group=quintile(stocks, "size", ["month"]))
independent = by_size.with_columns(
    illiq_group=quintile(by_size, "illiq", ["month"])
)
dependent = by_size.with_columns(
    illiq_group=quintile(by_size, "illiq", ["month", "size_group"])
)
```

## Compare monthly returns

For each size group, take the monthly return on its most illiquid quintile
minus that on its most liquid quintile. The table reports average spreads
in percentage points per month.

```{python}
def portfolio_returns(grouped):
    return (
        grouped
        .group_by("month", "size_group", "illiq_group")
        .agg(
            equal_weighted=pl.col("ret").mean(),
            value_weighted=(pl.col("ret") * pl.col("size")).sum() / pl.col("size").sum(),
        )
    )

def spread(returns):
    keys = ["month", "size_group"]
    low = returns.filter(pl.col("illiq_group") == 1).select(*keys, "equal_weighted", "value_weighted")
    high = returns.filter(pl.col("illiq_group") == 5).select(*keys, "equal_weighted", "value_weighted")
    return high.join(low, on=keys, suffix="_low", validate="1:1").select(
        *keys,
        equal_weighted=pl.col("equal_weighted") - pl.col("equal_weighted_low"),
        value_weighted=pl.col("value_weighted") - pl.col("value_weighted_low"),
    )

sorts = {"Independent": independent, "Dependent": dependent}
portfolios = {name: portfolio_returns(grouped) for name, grouped in sorts.items()}
spreads = pl.concat(
    spread(ret).with_columns(sort=pl.lit(name)) for name, ret in portfolios.items()
)

(
    spreads.group_by("sort", "size_group")
    .agg(
        months=pl.len(),
        equal_weighted_pct=(100 * pl.col("equal_weighted").mean()).round(3),
        value_weighted_pct=(100 * pl.col("value_weighted").mean()).round(3),
    )
    .sort("sort", "size_group")
)
```

Under the independent sort, a size–illiquidity cell can be sparse when the
characteristics are strongly related. The `months` column counts only
months in which both extremes have a return. The dependent sort gives an
illiquidity ranking separately within each size group, so it answers a
different question even though both designs use the same stocks.

```{python}
#| include: false

import os

if checkout := os.environ.get("ANOMALYLAB_CHECKOUT"):
    import sys
    from pathlib import Path

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(checkout).expanduser().resolve(strict=True)))
    from anomalylab import Panel

    reference = Panel(
        stocks.sort("month", "permno").to_pandas(),
        id="permno", time="month", frequency="M", ret="ret",
    )
    id_cols = ["month", "permno"]
    group_cols = ["size_group", "illiq_group"]
    for name, grouped in sorts.items():
        mode = name.lower()
        expected = (
            reference.group("ret", "size", ["size", "illiq"], [5, 5], sort_type=mode)
            .rename(columns={"size_g5": "size_group", "illiq_g5": "illiq_group"})
            [id_cols + group_cols]
            .sort_values(id_cols).reset_index(drop=True)
        )
        observed = grouped.select(*id_cols, *group_cols).sort(id_cols).to_pandas()
        observed["month"] = observed["month"].dt.to_period("M")
        pd.testing.assert_frame_equal(observed, expected, check_dtype=False)

        result = portfolios[name]
        monthly_keys = ["month", "size_group"]
        raw = result.to_pandas()
        raw["month"] = raw["month"].dt.to_period("M")
        hml = spread(result).to_pandas()
        hml["month"] = hml["month"].dt.to_period("M")
        ew, vw = reference.bivariate_analysis(
            "ret", "size", "size", "illiq", 5, 5, sort_type=mode, factor_return=True
        )
        errors = {}
        for col, reference_return in [("equal_weighted", ew), ("value_weighted", vw)]:
            actual = raw.pivot(index=monthly_keys, columns="illiq_group", values=col)
            actual["H-L"] = hml.set_index(monthly_keys)[col]
            expected = reference_return[
                reference_return.index.get_level_values("size").isin(range(1, 6))
            ].loc[:, [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, "H-L"]]
            expected.index = expected.index.set_names(monthly_keys)
            assert set(actual.index) == set(expected.index)
            actual = actual.reindex(expected.index)
            np.testing.assert_allclose(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
            errors[col] = np.nanmax(np.abs(actual.to_numpy() - expected.to_numpy()))
        print(f"{name}: {grouped.height:,} memberships, {result.height:,} portfolio-months; "
              f"maximum absolute difference: {errors}", file=sys.stderr)
```
